statement: Morgan Stanley expects server memory contract prices to rise more than 25% quarter-over-quarter in Q3 2026, with HBM capacity effectively sold out through 2026 and much of 2027 already pre-booked.
why: Memory is a hard input constraint for AI accelerators; sold-out HBM capacity and steeply rising contract prices mean GPU makers face both tighter supply and higher bill-of-materials cost, which caps how fast systems can ship.

impact.mechanism: HBM sold out through 2026 with 2027 pre-booked, plus 25%+ quarterly contract price increases, tightens the memory bottleneck feeding accelerator assembly and raises input cost for every accelerator program.

evidence.source: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'"
evidence.excerpt: server memory contract prices will climb more than 25% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter

evidence.source: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'"
evidence.excerpt: HBM production capacity is reportedly effectively sold out through 2026, with a significant portion of 2027 output already pre-booked

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet relaying a Morgan Stanley forecast; no filing-grade evidence and no separately fetched corroborating publishers, so capped at medium.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 2 -> 3; sources: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'", DIGITIMES — "Memory shortage to worsen in 2027 as AI inference strains supply"
